newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows drop in approval for NJ Governor.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows drop in approval for NJ Governor.

text.p: Gov. Christine Whitman's approval rating dropped sharply in recent weeks, although she would still defeat any of her possible Democratic challengers, according to a poll released Thursday.

Whitman's overall approval rating dropped 10 percentage points to 52 percent from February, in part because of skepticism about her handling of the state budget and taxes, the poll by Quinnipiac College of Hamden, Conn., found.

"Until this latest poll, she had been riding high," said Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Polling Institute. "Now, questions about her budget and tax plans cut into her overall approval and favorability rating."
On her handling of taxes, the poll revealed that Whitman had a negative rating of 42 to 54 percent, down from a positive rating of 49 to 46 percent in February.
Whitman gained national prominence for cutting state income taxes 30 percent.
Pollsters said part of the decline on the tax issue resulted from opposition to Whitman's proposal to borrow nearly $3 billion to pay off debts run up by the state's pension system.
About 49 percent of those surveyed called the borrowing plan "a gimmick to balance the state budget," while 19 percent said it is "good financial management."
Quinnipiac College surveyed 867 New Jersey residents who said they were registered voters. The poll was conducted April 1 through 6, and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percent.

The governor's spokesman Peter McDonough said the decline in approval can be attributed to her proposals being "an incredibly complicated message. Once we get engaged (in the campaign) this will turn around."
Whitman had a comfortable leads of 16 to 20 percentage points over three potential opponents in the November election, the poll found.
